오늘 챙겨야 할 해외 이슈

1. 잭슨홀 심포지엄에서의 파월 의장 연설 내용과 정책 경로 힌트 연준 인사들(슈미드, 해맥, 콜린스 등)이 인플레이션 지속 위험과 정책 제약성 부족을 경고하는 가운데, 시장은 파월 의장이 금리 인상 조건이나 반응 함수를 명확히 제시할지 주목하고 있다. 기사들은 그의 발언이 모호할 경우 장기 국채 매도세(30년물 금리 5.5% 상향 돌파 가능성)를 촉발하거나, 반대로 비둘기적 톤 시 변동성을 키울 수 있다고 지적한다. 재무부의 바이백 확대 계획이 연준 메시지와 상충할 수 있다는 점도 금리 변동성 확대의 배경이다. 2. 미국 7월 PCE 물가 및 핵심 지표가 가리키는 9월·10월 금리 인상 확률 변화 헤드라인 PCE 전년비 3.7%, 핵심 PCE 3.3%로 목표치 상회가 확인되었고, 서비스 물가 강세와 소득 증가세 지속이 인플레이션 완화 속도에 의문을 제기한다. 선물 시장은 9월 인상 확률을 42% 수준에서 반영 중이나, 향후 고용(CPI, 비농업고용) 지표가 더 결정적일 전망이다. 연준 인사 다수가 "현재 정책이 충분히 제약적인지 불확실"하다고 평가해 데이터 의존도가 한층 높아진 상황이다. 3. 에너지 가격 충격의 실물 경제 전이와 디젤 크랙 스프레드 급등 캔자스시티 연은 슈미드 총재가 "에너지 충격이 경제 전반으로 확산 중"이라고 경고한 가운데, 미국 디젤 크랙 스프레드가 배럴당 100달러를 넘어서는 등 정제 마진 급등이 국내 인플레이션 상방 압력으로 작용하고 있다. 국제 유가는 호르무즈 해협 협상 진전으로 하방 압력을 받으나, 러시아-우크라이나 확전 위험과 이란 제재 불확실성이 상존해 원자재발 인플레이션 리스크가 잔존한다. 4. 글로벌 재정 건전성 우려와 주요국 중앙행보의 매파적 편향 동시 발생 프랑스의 부채 급증과 고금리 부담, 독일 이포 지수 개선에도 ECB 슈나벨 이사의 추가 인상 시사, 캐나다 GDP 반등 기대 속 미-캐 무역 긴장 등 주요국에서 재정·통화 정책 불확실성이 동반 상승 중이다. 달러 인덱스는 수익률 연계가 약화된 상태이나, 잭슨홀 발언과 향후 지표에 따라 강세 전환 여부가 갈릴 전망이다. 5. 엔비디아 실적 발표 후 기술주 랠리 지속성과 광범위 시장 참여도(브레드스) 괴리 엔비디아 호실적에 힘입어 나스닥이 상승했으나, S&P500과 다우가 보합권에 머무르고 타 섹터가 하락하는 등 상승 폭이 기술 대형주에 극도로 집중되어 있다. AI 설비투자 사이클 연장 기대가 리스크 온 심리를 지지하지만, 연준 매파 발언과 금리 상승 시 고평가 기술주 밸류에이션 부담이 커질 수 있어 시장 내부 에너지 분포 변화를 모니터링할 필요가 있다.

Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh delivers his key Jackson Hole speech Friday
Jeff Cox · 2026-08-27T00:00:00.000Z

Summary: - Fed Chair Kevin Warsh is delivering the keynote at the Jackson Hole symposium. Markets are eagerly awaiting whether he will outline conditions for future rate moves and provide clearer guidance, given his prior hands-off, market-driven approach. - Warsh’s tenure has featured less forward guidance and more emphasis on letting markets interpret data, drawing mixed reviews. Investors fear ambiguity could trigger volatility, especially if his remarks are cryptic or sparse on reaction functions. - Rising Treasury yields heighten the stakes. Analysts expect Warsh to signal a willingness to raise rates if inflation remains unmoderated; otherwise, a dovish or non-committal tone could spur a sell-off in long-dated Treasurys, potentially pushing the 30-year yield above 5.5%. - Treasury actions complicate the backdrop: the Treasury plans to double buybacks of off-the-run debt, which could conflict with Warsh’s messaging and market expectations. - The speech is viewed as potentially the most important remarks of Warsh’s tenure, with readers hoping for clarity on policy path, rather than broad structural themes.

As Jackson Hole conference kicks off, three Fed officials warn about inflation | 740 The FAN

Summary: - Federal Reserve officials at Jackson Hole warn inflation remains a risk. 오늘 스냅샷은 위험자산군(주식·암호화폐)이 일제히 홀드에 머무는 가운데 안전자산군 역시 채권(TLT·IEF)이 홀드로 전환해 매도 압력을 내려놓았고, 통화(UUP)만 지속적인 매도 신호로 달러 약세 기조를 유지하고 있어 위험 선호·회피 간의 뚜렷한 대립보다는 관망세가 우세한 모습이다; 최근 2주간 주식과 비트코인이 8월 중순 동반 매수에서 홀드로 후퇴했고, 금(GLD)도 매수→홀드로 돌아서며 인플레이션 헤지 수요가 잦아든 반면, 농산물(DBA)은 8월 26일 매수 진입 후 홀로 매수를 유지해 여타 원자재(에너지·금속)와 뚜렷한 괴리를 보이고 있다 — 전반적으로 주요 자산군이 동반 홀드·매도 청산으로 수렴하며 방향성 탐색 국면에 진입했음을 시사한다.

DBA농산물 (Agriculture)매수종가 28.82
추천: 매수 **근거:** 기계적 규칙상 **종가(28.82)가 20일 돈치안 채널 상단을 상향 돌파(진입 시그널 True)했고, 청산 조건인 트레일링 스탑(28.07) 위로 확실하게 머물러 있으며, 거래량 급증까지 동반**되어 정석적인 추세추종 매수 신호가 완성됐다. 일목균형표 역시 구름 위·양운으로 정배열돼 보조 지표도 방향성을 지지한다. 뉴스 펀더멘털은 이 돌파가 단순한 기술적 반등이 아니라 **구조적 공급 위기(Supply Shock)에 의한 본격적 불장 진입**임을 뒷받침한다. 가장 관련성 높은 두 기사를 구체적으로 짚는다. 1. **ADM Investor Services / Pro Farmer (8/26 마감 코멘트)** - **옥수수**: 미국 작황 등급이 57% G/E로 예상을 하회, 프로파머 투어 추정 수확량(10.9 t/ha)이 USDA 전망(11.3)을 크게 밑돈다. 12월물 신고가 경신, 펀드 순매수 포지션이 32만 계약(3개월래 최대)으로 급증. - **밀**: 흑해 물류 차질(노보로시스크 항만 수리 1~4개월, 다뉴브 운하 정체) + 우크라이나 가뭄/러시아 수출 제한 우려로 일일 상한가 근접, 신고가 랠리. - **대두**: USDA 플래시 세일 13.2만 톤 확인, 크러시 마진 5개월 저점에도 불구하고 수요 낙관 유지. → DBA 포트폴리오의 핵심 비중(옥수수·밀·대두 합산 ≈ 60% 이상)을 차지하는 3대 곡물이 **동시에 공급 측 타이트니스·펀드 롱 포지션 확대·수출 물류 병목**이라는 ‘강세 3박자’를 갖추고 있어, 20일 돌파가 추세 개시로 이어질 개연성이 매우 높다. 2. **Citi “Super El Niño Risk Raises Grain Targets” (브라이언 맥콜)** - NOAA 기준 10~12월 ‘슈퍼 엘니뇨’ 확률 90% 이상, 1950년 이후 최강 가능성 69%. - 3개월/12개월 목표가 상향: 옥수수 $5.40→$5.90, 대두 $12.75→$13.25, 밀 $7.25→$7.75. - 팜유·로부스타 커피·설탕·코코아·호주 밀 등 소프트 원자재까지 ‘생산 위험(Production-at-Risk)’ 프레임으로 동반 상승 전망. → 단기 기상 이변이 중장기 공급 곡선을 좌우하는 **매크로 강세장 진입**을 시사하며, DBA 바스켓 전반(곡물+소프트+축산)에 걸친 광범위한 상승 모멘텀을 제공한다. **리스크 관리 코멘트**: 일목 구름 위·양운이라 추가 진입 비중 축소 불필요. 시스템대로 **초기 진입 후 트레일링 스탑(28.07)만 기계적으로 추종**하면 된다.

Ag Market View for Aug 26.2026 - ADM Investor Services
Mark Soderberg · 2026-08-26T00:00:00.000Z

Ag Market View for Aug 26, 2026 (ADM Investor Services) - Key takeaways for agricultural commodities: Corn - Prices up ~0.08–0.10, closing near session highs; Sept-26 above $5 for first time in ~2.5 years. - Dec-26 hits new contract highs late in the session. - Crop ratings drop to 57% good/excellent (lower than expected); average US yield forecast around 180.1 bpa with production ~15.953 bb, about 60 mbu below USDA forecast. - Fund positioning: non-commercials' net long ~321k contracts (likely >330k post-session), largest in 3 months. - EU corn yield estimate lowered ~5% to 6.61 mt/ha; Brazil 2025/26 second crop 92% harvested, 1st crop planting for 26/27 underway. - Seasonal note: December corn has not peaked in October since 1980. Soybeans - Beans higher by ~0.12–0.14; meal steady to +$1; bean oil +40–50 points. - First resistance for Nov-26 around $12.44½, then $12.56½ (weekly highs). - Soybean oil weakness attributed to EPA SRE relief expectations for RINs (up to $1.8b). D4 RINs recent lows ~ $1.92. - Crush margins near 5-month low; USDA flash soybean sale of 132k mt supports demand optimism. - Crop ratings down 1% to 60% G/E; composite ratings weakest of the cycle; pods setting at 91%. Wheat (CGO/KC) - Prices spike to daily limit, CGO Dec-26 potentially trading above limit; new contract highs for CGO and KC. - Technicals indicate strong upside risk: next resistance around CGO $7.77¼, KC $8.58. - Global logistics: Russia’s Novorossiysk port repairs (1–4 months) and port access bottlenecks impacting grain exports; Danube/Sulina Canal vessel delays. - Ukraine winter wheat plantings at risk due to drought; Russia hints at export measures; Egypt and other buyers boosting imports; EU soft wheat exports down ~33% YoY; Sudan buys French wheat. Overall outlook - Bullish near-term momentum in corn and wheat; soybeans supported by a new soybean sale and residual demand optimism. - Watch for ongoing supply-side developments (US crop ratings, Brazil/Ukraine/Russia logistics, EPA RIN policy) as primary drivers in the near term. - Key levels to monitor: Corn futures above $5 (Sept), Dec-26 highs; Soybeans resistance near $12.44–$12.56; CGO/KC targets near $7.77¼ and $8.58.

Citi Elevates Grain Targets as Super El Nino Risk Rises
Brian McColl · 2026-08-25T11:29:48.000Z

Citi’s agricultural outlook argues for a bullish tilt in grains and select soft commodities into late 2026/early 2027, driven by a stronger-than-expected Super El Niño and multiple catalysts. Key points: - El Niño risk: NOAA data shows >90% probability of a very strong El Niño and a 69% chance it surpasses all since 1950 in Oct–Dec, underpinning the adverse weather scenario Citi foresees for global crops. - Price targets raised: Citi lifts 3-month and 12-month targets for corn, soybeans, and wheat: - Corn: 3m $5.40/bu; 12m $5.90/bu - Soybeans: 3m $12.75/bu; 12m $13.25/bu - Wheat: 3m $7.25/bu; 12m $7.75/bu - Production-at-Risk framework: Prices may understate downside risk to global production; Citi’s framework suggests more potential upside for prices from weather, El Niño, and supply disruptions. - Commodities most exposed to weather risk: Palm oil, robusta coffee, rice, sugar, cocoa, and Australian wheat are highlighted as highly vulnerable, with regional concentration in Australia, India, Southeast Asia, and parts of Brazil. - Weather/geopolitics as drivers: A confluence of weaker yields, strong export demand, Black Sea disruptions, fertilizer/energy costs, and biofuel demand supports a bullish thesis for agriculture. - Wheat sensitivity: Wheat is identified as the most sensitive grain to the combined weather and geopolitical risks, with recent European heat/drought cutting production estimates. Bottom line: Citi expects higher upside for key grains and several tropical/soft commodities due to an escalating El Niño-driven weather risk and correlated supply concerns, with the strongest implications for corn, soybeans, wheat, palm oil, and robutas coffee, especially in the affected regions.

Global corn market surges, driven by US, Europe crop concerns | Farm Online | ACT
www.farmonline.com.au · 2026-08-26T00:00:00.000Z

Global corn leads the recent agricultural commodities rally as weather and crop conditions raise supply concerns in key regions. Key points: - Corn (Chicago futures) up ~4% for the week and ~5% for the month, driven by deteriorating US crop conditions: USDA ratings at 57% good-to-excellent, and Pro Farmer tour yield at 10.9 t/ha vs USDA 11.3 t/ha anticipated. - Market questions whether US production forecasts are overly optimistic amid tighter supply. - Europe faces worsening maize outlook due to heat and drought; EU crop monitors cut maize yield to 6.61 t/ha, ~7% below the five-year average; EU soybean and sunflower yields also below average. - Monsoon in India weak, reinforcing global supply concerns; wheat remains supported but less volatile amid Black Sea export disruption and ample Russian supply. - Overall market dynamic: corn emerges as the lead grain due to weather-driven risk, with wheat activity more restrained; Black Sea disruptions persist but do not create a full-scale shortage signal yet. - Australia-specific context: regional variability in crop prospects (South Australia strong; parts of WA vulnerable); local prices down in several ports; input costs easing slightly but fertilizer remains below year-ago levels. - Outlook drivers to watch: September rainfall impacts on soybeans, corn, and pulses; soil moisture and spring rainfall influencing late-season wheat and rapeseed planting. Implications for outlook: - The global corn complex is the primary driver of near-term price action due to US and European weather risk. - Wheat remains supported but less volatile; regional disruptions and shipping flows continue to shape prices. - Fertilizer costs easing modestly provides some input-cost relief, but macro weather risk remains the dominant factor for crop markets.

A Speculation On Why Global Food Markets Are Rallying | RealClearMarkets
Imran Khalid · 2026-08-23T00:00:00.000Z

Summary: The article argues that global food markets are rallying not because physical scarcity is imminent, but due to psychology and policy-driven supply anticipation. Key points: - Global food inflation could rise from ~2.8% (H1 2026) to ~5% (H1 2027) as vulnerabilities in supply chains (notably fertilizer) surface. A major risk is the Gulf fertiliser chokepoint (half of world urea supply) and possible prolonged disruption. - El Niño (likely to intensify) could push acutely food-insecure people from 225 million to about 274 million, with sharp regional impacts (Central America, Southern Africa). This supports elevated risk premiums. - Market mechanics: bullish sentiment can pull futures up before physical scarcity materializes. Governments preemptively stockpile and restrict exports (e.g., China on phosphate, Russia on urea/DAP) while others sign bilateral deals, creating a divergence between perceived scarcity and actual on-hand inventories. - FAO data suggests 2026 cereal production remains high (2.983 billion tonnes; only ~1.9% below 2025) with stock-to-use near 32%, indicating tight pockets rather than a global shortage. Wheat declines exist due to drought; maize is stronger in other regions. - National responses indicate hedging against volatility: price supports and reserves (China), ongoing output expansion (Brazil), European Fertiliser Action Plan, and bilateral supply pacts (Philippines, Singapore) to improve resilience. - The near-term price moves are driven by sentiment and hedging gaps between reported inventory and perceived scarcity, rather than immediate stockouts. The market is currently leaning on sentiment more than physical inventories, though reserve-building quietly narrows the gap. Bottom line for agricultural commodities market outlook: - Expect continued volatility driven by supply-chain bottlenecks, fertilizer constraints, and El Niño risks. - Bulls may persist as traders price in potential shortages, even if current stocks appear adequate in many regions. - Policy actions and bilateral supply agreements could mitigate some risk but may also tighten liquidity in global markets. The divergence between sentiment-driven futures and actual on-hand inventories remains a key watch item.

UUP미국 달러 인덱스 (US Dollar Index)매도종가 28.02
추천: 매도 **근거:** 1. **기계적 청산 규칙 발동 (최우선):** 현재 종가(28.02)가 트레일링 스탑(28.03) 아래로 명백히 하향 이탈했습니다(`청산 시그널: True`). 추세추종 시스템에서 '수익 보호'와 '손실 제한'을 위한 유일한 청산 규칙이 작동한 것이므로, 뉴스나 보조지표 해석과 무관하게 즉시 보유 물량을 청산(매도)해야 합니다. 20일/100일 돌파 신호도 모두 `False`라 재진입 조건도 성립하지 않습니다. 2. **뉴스 팩트가 청산 신호를 뒷받침함:** 수집된 기사들(BBH, ING, Convera, TMGM, FXStreet)은 공통적으로 **달러 인덱스(DXY)가 200일 이동평균선(~99.17~99.75) 부근에서 강한 저항을 받으며 상향 돌파에 실패하고 있다**는 기술적·펀더멘털 사실을 전합니다. - **BBH 기사**는 "인플레이션은 끈적하지만 가속되지 않고, 실질 소비가 둔화되어 연준이 공격적 긴축 대신 금리 동결 여지를 갖는다"며 **'비둘기적 재평가(Dovish Repricing)' 시 달러 약세 취약**을 경고했습니다. 시장이 9월 인상 확률을 36~42% 수준으로만 반영 중이라 추가 모멘텀이 약합니다. - **TMGM 기사**는 "200일 EMA(99.75)가 핵심 캡(Cap) 역할을 하며, 일봉 종가 기준 상향 돌파 전까지는 약세 편향이 유효하다"고 명시했습니다. UUP 종가 28.02는 DXY 환산 시 99 초반대로, 이 저항대 하단에서 밀려나는 흐름과 정확히 일치합니다. - **ING·Convera** 역시 워시(Kevin Warsh) 잭슨홀 연설이 '매파적 서프라이즈' 없으면 달러 상승분을 반납할 재료라고 일관되게 지적합니다. 즉, **펀더멘털상 추가 상승 동력(매수세)이 소진되고 하방 압력이 우세한 국면**이라, 트레일링 스탑 하향 이탈은 단순한 노이즈가 아니라 추세 전환의 시작 신호로 읽힙니다. 3. **일목균형표(보조 참고) 상충 시 리스크 관리:** 현재 `구름 안 · 양운(상승 구름)`으로, 중장기 추세는 아직 상승 쪽으로 해석될 여지가 있습니다. 이는 기계적 매도 신호와 **엇갈리는 보조 정보**입니다. 시스템 원칙상 이 정보로 매도 추천을 번복하지는 않으나, **'추세 전환 초기일 수 있으니 청산 후 즉시 역추세(숏) 진입은 자제하고, 20일/100일 하단 돌파나 구름 하향 이탈 등 명확한 하락 확인 신호가 나올 때까지 관망'**하는 것이 리스크 관리상 타당합니다. **요약:** 규칙(종가 < 트레일링 스탑)이 매도를 명령하고, 뉴스 팩트(200일선 저항·연준 비둘기적 선회 가능성·모멘텀 소진)가 그 신호의 신뢰도를 높여줍니다. 보조지표(양운)만 보고 홀딩을 고집하면 '규칙 기반 기계적 매매' 원칙을 위배하는 것이므로, **즉시 매도(청산) 후 현금 보유**를 권고합니다.

US Dollar: Fed repricing risk weighs on usd – BBH
www.fxstreet.com · 2026-08-27T00:00:00.000Z

BBH commentary on the US dollar outlook: - The USD remains consolidating after recent gains, with the DXY testing its 200-day moving average around 99.17. - Core drivers: PCE inflation is above the Fed’s 2% target while real consumer spending is weakening, giving the Fed room to hold rates instead of tightening aggressively. - Fed pricing: Markets still price only modest tightening ahead (around 40 basis points total over the next year; roughly 36% odds of a 25bp hike at the Sept meeting). - Peso on the Fed: The stance described as dovish for the dollar—fewer near-term rate hikes could weaken the USD as expectations shift. - Broader context: The Jackson Hole gathering starts, with potential limited forward guidance from Fed Chair Warsh; markets will watch for communications framework, balance sheet, and inflation strategies from the Fed’s task forces. - Commodity and tech note: Brent under $90, Nvidia earnings reinforce AI-driven capex backdrop, contributing to risk-on sentiment that can support a softer dollar if USD repricing begins. In short, BBH sees the dollar as vulnerable to a dovish repricing given sticky but non-accelerating inflation and softening real spending, with markets unlikely to price in aggressive Fed tightening in the near term. The DXY faces resistance near the 200-day moving average, but the outcome hinges on Fed messaging post-Jackson Hole.

US Dollar: Warsh speech keeps markets cautious – ING
www.fxstreet.com · 2026-08-27T00:00:00.000Z

Summary: The ING view ahead of Jackson Hole remains cautiously bearish for the US dollar, though risks tilt the other way on hawkish shifts. Key takeaways: - PCE data show disinflation intact but still gradual. Core PCE at 0.2% MoM / 3.3% YoY; headline PCE at 0.2% MoM / 3.7% YoY. Inflation trends support a hold but keep rate hikes on the table less likely. - The Fed is expected to hold rates on 16 September. ING expects a weaker dollar on a balance of data and Fed guidance, but acknowledges hawkish pricing around Warsh’s Jackson Hole speech could lift DXY toward 99.0. - Data mix: July real spending flat as households save more; real disposable income flatlining for over a year. This soft growth backdrop favors a hold path, though markets price ~50% odds of a hike by decision day, which could rise with further hawkish signals. - Warsh’s Jackson Hole speech is a potential catalyst. If markets read his remarks as hawkish, dollar upside could re-emerge despite a general hold scenario. - FX implications: EUR/USD hovering around 1.1650 amid uncertain USD direction; risk sentiment and Nvidia-like upside can provide some USD support, but the broader bias remains toward a weaker dollar if the Fed stays on hold and data keep disinflation on track. - Near-term focus: Jackson Hole remarks and the upcoming NFP revision; markets may not want to push USD shorts aggressively ahead of Warsh, keeping DXY supported around 99.0 ahead of the event. Bottom line for DXY: The macro setup leans toward a hold in September and a softer dollar, but Jackson Hole and any hawkish Fedspeak could briefly prop up the dollar and push DXY toward 99.0. The longer-term bias remains a weaker dollar if the data keep inflation slowly trending down and the Fed maintains a cautious stance.

US data keeps Fed hawks in play | Convera
Kevin Ford · 2026-08-26T00:00:00.000Z

Summary: The US dollar's near-term direction remains unclear, as mixed inflation data and geopolitics keep Fed hawks engaged but not decisively moving the dollar. Key points for the DXY: - Inflation data: July PCE rose modestly (headline +0.2%, +3.7% y/y; core PCE in line). Services inflation firm. This supports a cautious, hawkish Fed stance but not a clear trigger for a rally. - Growth and demand: GDP at 1.5% with solid durable goods (driven by transport) and wage-income dynamics improving household savings. The data has not shifted the probability of a September hike meaningfully (markets price roughly a 42% chance). - Yield/curves: Two-year yield rose on firm inflation, but long end contained by Treasury buybacks, steepening the curve and weakening the traditional yield-dollar link. - Warsh influence: A hawkish or vague Jackson Hole signal from Kevin Warsh could lift the DXY toward 99.50–100.00; ambiguity could leave payrolls/CPI as the main drivers. - Geopolitical and fiscal risk: Hormuz-related developments and US fiscal credibility concerns add downside pressure on the dollar; gold’s strength (~14% monthly) signals risk hedging rather than pure policy expectations. - USD/CAD dynamics: USD/CAD sits in a 1.3760–1.3900 range, with 1.3900 as key resistance. A break above 1.3900 could push toward 1.4000–1.4100; a break below 1.3760 could target 1.3500–1.3700. Canadian data (Q2 GDP) and US policy signals will shape the pair. - Near-term guidance: Rates are currently the clearest near-term indicator for USD direction. A credible hawkish Warsh message could support the dollar; in the absence of clarity, payrolls and CPI will be decisive for September expectations. Bottom line: The DXY is consolidating near 99.00 with limited momentum. The next move hinges on Warsh’s Jackson Hole guidance and upcoming payrolls/CPI data, with risk skewed by geopolitics and fiscal concerns. In the immediate term, a test of 98.80 support or a push toward 99.50–100.00 remains contingent on new inflation signals and policy cues.
